Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is the mutual action plan (LD-9823_MAP_v1.1.pdf) that outlines the evaluation checkpoints, acceptance criteria, and a short performance benchmarking plan focused on the embeddings + reranker endpoints. High level:

- Goal: confirm production-grade latency and throughput for the embedding -> reranker flow under your target concurrency (50/100/200 concurrent users). Verify TTFT (time-to-first-token) and p95 latency for reranker ranking on 512-token contexts.
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed): p50 <= 60ms (embed), p95 <= 250ms (reranker end-to-end) for 100 concurrent sessions, sustained throughput >= 120 QPS for reranker.
- Evaluation steps: small-scale baseline (single-GPU), scale-up load tests (autoscaling profile), and localized stress run during your peak window.
- Deliverables: test harness, raw CSV of per-request latencies (perf-results-emb-rerank-20270104.csv), and a summary slide with recommended config (quantization + batching).

Can you confirm the target concurrency you'd like us to prioritize (you mentioned 100 concurrent earlier) and the preferred window for full load tests next Monday? Once confirmed, Aditya will share the exact endpoint names, model variants, and the test run times.

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks — locking in the Monday window. Quick technical notes and what we'll run: 

- Endpoints: /v1/embeddings/atlas-embed-v2 (fp16) -> /v1/rerank/atlas-rerank-v1 (quantized int8). We'll provide pinned model versions in the test harness.
- Test harness: Locally hosted k6 scripts for traffic shaping, deterministic seed for query set (2k queries representative of your production distribution), and configurable concurrency stages: ramp 0->100 in 5 minutes, steady 30 minutes, ramp to 200 for 10 minutes (stress).
- Metrics we collect: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), TTFT for reranker (open-stream first-token), end-to-end embed+rerank wall time, CPU/GPU utilization, NVLink saturation, GPU memory headroom, and token throughput (tokens/sec).
- Pass/fail: we'll add SLO flags: green if p95 <= 250ms at 100 conc; yellow if 250ms < p95 <= 350ms; red if p95 > 350ms or error rate > 1%.
- Cost estimate: incremental GPU hours for the 200-concurrency stress run is ~9 GPU-hours on our Dedicated cluster; rough cost uplift estimate $1.2k (we'll send detailed breakouts post-run).

I'll attach the raw CSV and a short summary after the run. Any objections to the pass/fail buckets above?

- Aditya
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Priya / Tom —

We completed the runs at 10:30–11:45 PST (baseline + 100-concurrency steady + 200-concurrency stress). Aditya attached the raw CSV; summary below. We'll meet at 15:30 PST to walk through details.

Summary (key metrics):
- Embeddings (atlas-embed-v2, fp16):
  - p50: 43ms, p95: 89ms, throughput at 100 conc: ~340 QPS
- Reranker (atlas-rerank-v1, int8, end-to-end including embed):
  - 100 concurrency steady: p50 78ms, p95 238ms, p99 410ms; sustained throughput 128 QPS; TTFT median 22ms
  - 200 concurrency stress: p50 105ms, p95 392ms, p99 760ms; sustained throughput 210 QPS; error rate 0.9% (transient queue timeouts)
- Resource notes: GPUs averaged 67% utilization during 100 conc; NVLink spikes at ~72% during 200 conc. KV cache hit ratio was 46% for this query mix.

Pass/fail verdict (per agreed buckets):
- 100-concurrency: GREEN (p95 238ms <= 250ms, error rate <1%)
- 200-concurrency: YELLOW (p95 392ms > 350ms but error rate ~0.9%)

Next steps / recommendations:
1) For production at steady 100 concurrent users: pin atlas-rerank-v1 (int8) with batching config: max_batch_size=64, batch_delay_ms=8; enable prefix KV caching and 1.5x autoscaling headroom.
2) For burst tolerance to 200 conc: recommend moving to a 2x cluster headroom (or use Dedicated burst nodes) and enable a fallback to a slightly smaller reranker variant for best-effort p95 under heavy burst.
3) We'll provide an itemized cost uplift for the 200-concurrency profile by EOD.

Attaching: perf-results-emb-rerank-20270104.csv and the MAP PDF in case you need it.

Thanks — see you at 15:30.

Soojin
